clue.text: Appellation created by President Lincoln in the fifties

indicators.note: the president is placed inside the two fifties, so in signals containment here

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them give LL
Abe was the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A historian claims some name was coined by Abraham Lincoln during the 1850s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fifties' reads as a decade, but it means two Roman fifties, one either side of the president.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a name or designation given to something, which is what an appellation is.

clue.text: Two notes that follow so delayed

wordplay.note: in tonic sol-fa the scale runs do, re, mi, fa, so and then two more notes before do returns; those two are taken in order

explanation.surface: Something arrives behind schedule because it trails behind another thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' is not a link word here but the fifth note of the sol-fa scale; la and te come after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something late has arrived after the expected time, so it has been held up.

clue.text: Optimal to live above street

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
ST is the usual abbreviation in addresses

explanation.surface: Advice that the ideal home is a flat over a shop on the high street.
explanation.definitionFit: The best option is the most favourable one, which is the optimal choice.

clue.text: Oil that's but a relic, sadly

explanation.definitionFit: To lubricate a machine is to apply oil or grease so its parts move smoothly; here oil is a verb.

clue.text: Poultry cage Edward brought on board

parts.note: a coop is a cage or pen for hens

explanation.surface: A man named Edward is recruited to help with the hen house.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-opt someone is to appoint them onto a committee or team, recruiting them into the group.

clue.text: Racket smashing causes talk

parts.note: a racket is a swindle or scam, as is a con
smashing and fab are both informal words for excellent

explanation.surface: A noisy racket being smashed sets everyone gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like noise and 'smashing' looks like an anagram signal, but they are a fraud and a word of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab, short for confabulation, is an informal chat or discussion.

clue.text: Grass where go-carts oddly going missing

explanation.surface: A track where karts run off onto the grass verge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal crop, and cereals are botanically members of the grass family.

a rim is an edge or border
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'boat' with a stray space.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a vessel with three parallel hulls, an unusual design compared with a single-hulled craft.

clue.text: Breaks up gangs descended on by CID officers

clue.text: Weapons treaty, shaky at best, close to completion

parts.note: the word whose final letter is wanted

clue.text: Puts in order that requires instant mug shot first of all

parts.note: the five words whose initial letters are taken in order

taken as written
cola is a carbonated soft drink
taken as written

a lab is a place of practical work

clue.text: Unusual jade stud, fixed as required

clue.text: A maker of horror films needing someone to overact?

second meaning: read as ..., one who hams, playing a part too broadly

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a whimsical coinage: to ham is to overact, so a hammer is one who does it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a British horror studio and, jokingly, a performer who hams it up.

clue.text: Verbals duo exchanged in the streets of Paris?
